name: so … that, such … that, too, enough
subtitle: Say how strong something is and what follows from it: so … that and such … that give a result, too + adjective gives a limit, adjective + enough means "as much as you need". It was so hot that we stayed in. The bag is too heavy to carry.
source: icanspeak English original English text (grammar-b2 run, 2026-10-29)

concept.exampleHtml: It was so hot that we stayed in. · It was such a hot day that we stayed in. · It was too hot to go out. · It wasn't cool enough to go out.

qa.html: so + adjective / adverb + that shows how strong something is and what the result is: The film was so long that we left early. She spoke so quickly that I couldn't follow. With nouns use so much (uncountable) or so many (plural): There was so much traffic that we were late. In speech you can leave out that.

such (a/an) + (adjective) + noun + that says the same with a noun. Use a/an only with a singular countable noun: It was such a long film that we left early. We had such terrible weather that we stayed in. They are such good friends that they never argue. Rule of thumb: so before an adjective, such before a noun.

too + adjective means "more than is good or possible". It is negative: The tea is too hot. You can add for + person and to + verb: The bag is too heavy for me to carry. Do not repeat the object: not too heavy to carry it. With nouns: too much noise, too many cars.

adjective + enough means "as much as we need". Enough comes after an adjective or adverb: She is old enough to drive. He didn't run fast enough. Before a noun it comes first: We have enough chairs. I haven't got enough time to cook.

Typical mistakes: ✗ The tea is too much hot. → ✓ The tea is too hot. (too much only before a noun) · ✗ She isn't enough tall. → ✓ She isn't tall enough. (enough after the adjective) · ✗ It was so a nice day. → ✓ It was such a nice day. (a noun follows, so use such)

concept.noteHtml: too and enough are often followed by to + verb, see -ing or to. so … that (result) is not the same as so that (purpose): I spoke slowly so that she could understand. You find purpose clauses in purpose. too is not the same as very: very hot is a lot, too hot is a problem. For other ways to link a fact and its opposite, see contrast. Formal writing can use so … as to and such … as to, but you rarely need them.

tables.caption: The patterns
head: Pattern
Form
Example
rows: The soup was so hot that I couldn't eat it.
so much + uncountable, so many + plural + that
There were so many people that we couldn't get in.

too + adjective (+ for sb) (+ to + verb)
The soup is too hot for me to eat.
adjective + enough, enough + noun (+ to + verb)
She is old enough to drive. We have enough time.

listen.text: It was so cold that we stayed at home.
listen.note: so + adjective + that: the result comes after that.

listen.text: It was such a cold day that we stayed at home.
listen.note: such a + adjective + noun + that: the same idea with a noun.

listen.text: The bag is too heavy for me to carry.
listen.note: too + adjective + for sb + to + verb: no object after carry.

hoeren.instruction: Listen and choose the pattern you hear. You can listen twice.

items.text: The soup was so hot that I couldn't eat it.
It was such a long film that we left early.
The box is too heavy to lift.
She is old enough to drive.
We had such good weather that we swam every day.
There is too much noise to sleep.

rounds.label: 1 · so … that
rounds.instruction: You hear two short sentences. Join them with so … that. The second sentence is the result.

example.prompt: The room was hot. We opened the window.
example.answer: The room was so hot that we opened the window.

items.prompt: The music was loud. We couldn't talk.
items.answer: The music was so loud that we couldn't talk.

items.prompt: The bag was heavy. I couldn't lift it.
items.answer: The bag was so heavy that I couldn't lift it.

items.prompt: She was tired. She fell asleep at once.
items.answer: She was so tired that she fell asleep at once.

items.prompt: The queue was long. We gave up.
items.answer: The queue was so long that we gave up.

items.prompt: He drives fast. Nobody can follow him.
items.answer: He drives so fast that nobody can follow him.

items.prompt: The film was funny. We laughed all night.
items.answer: The film was so funny that we laughed all night.

rounds.label: 2 · so → such
rounds.instruction: You hear a sentence with so … that. Say it again with such … that and a noun.

example.prompt: The film was so long that we left early.
example.answer: It was such a long film that we left early.

items.prompt: The hotel was so cheap that we stayed a week.
items.answer: It was such a cheap hotel that we stayed a week.

items.prompt: The coffee was so strong that I couldn't sleep.
items.answer: It was such strong coffee that I couldn't sleep.

items.prompt: The book was so good that I read it twice.
items.answer: It was such a good book that I read it twice.

items.prompt: The test was so hard that nobody passed.
items.answer: It was such a hard test that nobody passed.

items.prompt: The weather was so nice that we ate outside.
items.answer: It was such nice weather that we ate outside.

items.prompt: The beach was so beautiful that we stayed all day.
items.answer: It was such a beautiful beach that we stayed all day.

exercises.title: so, such, too or enough? Complete the sentences.
exercises.hint: Look at the word after the gap: an adjective, a noun, or a/an + noun. Then look at how the sentence continues.
exercises.hintHtml: so+ adjective or adverb, then that: so hot thatsuch+ (a) + noun, then that: such a hot day thattoo+ adjective, a problem: too hot to drinkenoughafter an adjective, before a noun

items.prompt: The soup was ___ hot that I couldn't eat it.
items.why: An adjective (hot) follows and that gives the result: so.

items.prompt: It was ___ a hot day that we stayed inside.
items.why: A noun phrase follows (a hot day): such a + adjective + noun.

items.prompt: This bag is ___ heavy for me to carry.
items.why: More than I can manage, with for me to carry: too. Enough does not come before the adjective.

items.prompt: Are you old ___ to drive?
items.why: Enough comes after an adjective: old enough.

items.prompt: We have ___ chairs for everyone.
items.why: Enough comes before a noun and means as many as we need.

items.prompt: There were ___ many people that we couldn't get in.
items.why: so many + plural noun + that. Such is not used before many.

items.prompt: It was ___ good weather that we swam every day.
items.why: A noun follows (weather), so use such, not so.

items.prompt: The flat is ___ expensive for us to buy.
items.why: It is more expensive than we can pay: too + adjective + for us to buy.

exercises.title: Say it another way.
exercises.hint: Keep the meaning. Watch the word order and do not repeat the object after too … to.

rows.term: The tea was so hot that I couldn't drink it.
rows.answer: The tea was too hot to drink.
choices: The tea was too hot to drink.
The tea was too hot to drink it.
The tea was too much hot to drink.
The tea was hot enough to drink.

rows.term: The film was so boring that I fell asleep.
rows.answer: It was such a boring film that I fell asleep.

rows.term: She isn't tall, so she can't reach the shelf.
rows.answer: She isn't tall enough to reach the shelf.
choices: She isn't tall enough to reach the shelf.

She isn't too tall to reach the shelf.
She isn't so tall to reach the shelf.

rows.term: We had so much homework that we couldn't go out.
rows.answer: We had too much homework to go out.
choices: We had too much homework to go out.
We had too many homework to go out.
We had enough homework to go out.
We had too much of homework to go out.

rows.term: The bus was so full that we couldn't get on.
rows.answer: The bus was too full for us to get on.
choices: The bus was too full for us to get on.
The bus was too full to us getting on.
The bus was full enough for us to get on.
The bus was so full for us to get on.

exercises.title: Gap text: A day at the seaside.
exercises.hint: so, such, too or enough? Look at the word after the gap and at how the sentence continues.

segments.text: Priya and Kwame went to the beach in Brighton. It was
a sunny day that they left their jackets at home. The sea looked
blue that Kwame wanted to swim at once. But the water was
cold for Priya to get in. Kwame was brave
to swim for ten minutes. Afterwards the beach was
crowded that they had nowhere to sit. At lunch the café was
busy for them to find a table, so they ate their chips on the wall. It wasn't warm
to stay after six, so they went home.
